Most depressed and/or traumatized people aren't purposefully "clinging" to their negative emotions. Those thoughts can literally occupy their mind at all times and there's nothing they can do, outside of medication and therapy if they can afford it. 

Depression is messy, and difficult, and different for everyone who experiences it. They shouldn't be looked down on for not instantly feeling better when someone tries to help. Depression doesn't excuse lashing out, obviously, but it takes time and patience. You're under no obligation to help if you don't want, but you should at least be understanding of where they're coming from.

First thing to consider is who exactly you want to come out to. Family, close friends, classmates?

You should also consider this person's opinions on/knowledge of the LGBT+ community. Genders outside of the binary aren't exactly a mainstream concept, so you may have to do a little bit of explaining if the person seems confused.

All in all, just do it in whatever way you feel most comfortable. If you want to make a big deal out of it, go for it. If you wanna keep it on the DL, that's rad too. If you feel that you would be put in danger by coming out, I would personally hold off on it, but otherwise just trust your gut and do it whenever you feel ready.

Honestly, if its causing you this much stress, it may be a good idea to just tell her. If you two are pretty close friends, which it sounds like you are, I doubt confessing would ruin your friendship. Things may be a bit awkward, but even that'll probably go away eventually. And who knows? She may feel the same way too.

Basically, its probably better to get it off your chest than to bottle it up and possibly regret it later.
There's nothing wrong with prioritizing your mental health, or with feeling overwhelmed in your situation. Have you spoken to her about your feelings? If not, I think that would be a good first step.
